items.title: Section: Practising in Accordance With the Dharma Opens — Five Aspects, and What to Avoid, What to Do

items.zh: 云何菩薩法隨法行？當知此行略有五種。謂如所求、如所受法，身語意業無倒隨轉，正思、正修。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's practising in accordance with the dharma? This practice should be understood as, in brief, five kinds: in accordance with the dharma as sought and as received, the deeds of body, of speech, and of mind proceeding without error, together with correct thinking and correct cultivation.

items.zh: 若佛世尊於彼諸法，制身語意令不造作。於此諸法，開身語意令其造作。即於如是二種法中，身語意業無倒遠離、無倒修證。是名菩薩於諸法中，身語意業無倒隨轉法隨法行。
items.en: Whatever deeds the World-Honoured Buddha has prohibited of body, speech, and mind, one does not perform; whatever deeds of body, speech, and mind the Buddha has, regarding these other matters, opened and permitted, one does perform. Precisely within these two categories, keeping the deeds of body, speech, and mind free of error — rightly abstaining from the one, rightly cultivating and realising the other — this is called a bodhisattva's deeds of body, speech, and mind proceeding without error in practising in accordance with the dharma.

items.zh: 云何菩薩於法正思？

items.title: Section: Correct Thinking About the Dharma — Eight Marks Named

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩獨居閑靜，隨所聞法樂欲思惟、樂欲稱量、樂欲觀察。先當遠離不思議處，思惟彼法。恒常思惟，無間加行、殷重加行，而無慢緩。
items.en: Bodhisattvas dwell alone in quiet solitude, and, regarding whatever teaching has been heard, delight in reflecting on it, delight in weighing it through reasoning, and delight in observing it directly. First, one should steer clear of what should not be speculated upon, and reflect on the teaching within that boundary. One reflects constantly, applying oneself without interruption and with earnest care, never lax or slack.

items.zh: 是諸菩薩勇猛精進思惟法時，於其少分以理觀察而隨悟入。於其少分，但深信解。凡所思惟，但依其義，不依其文。如實了知黑說、大說。正能悟入最初思惟。既悟入已，數數作意令得堅固。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, thinking through the teaching with vigorous diligence, come to understand one portion through reasoned observation, entering it directly; and, for another portion, simply hold it through deep faith and understanding alone. In whatever they reflect on, they rely on the meaning, not on the literal wording. They rightly recognise what is left unspoken and what is spoken fully. They genuinely break through into a first, initial reflection; and, having broken through, apply repeated attention so that it becomes firm and stable.

items.title: The Benefit of Avoiding Confusion, and of Never Letting Understanding Slip

items.zh: 是諸菩薩由能遠離不應思議而思惟故，其心不墮迷悶錯亂。
items.en: Because bodhisattvas are able to steer clear of what should not be speculated upon while reflecting, their minds do not fall into confusion or disorder.

items.zh: 由能恒常無間、殷重加行無緩而思惟故，先未知義得正了知、得正決了，先已知義得無失壞、得不忘失。
items.en: Because one is able to reflect constantly, without interruption, applying oneself earnestly and never slackly, whatever meaning was not yet known comes to be rightly known and rightly settled, and whatever meaning was already known is never lost or destroyed, never forgotten.

items.title: Section: Insight That Needs No Outside Help, Faith That Never Slanders, and Meaning Over the Literal Word

items.zh: 由於少分以理觀察隨悟入故，於隨正理觀察法中，不由他緣。
items.en: Because one comes to understand a portion through reasoned observation, entering it directly, one no longer depends on any other condition when observing the teaching according to genuine reasoning.

items.zh: 由於少分但信解故，於極甚深自少覺慧不能達法，仰推如來，言如是法是佛所行，非我境界。如是於法不生誹謗，不自損害，遠離衰患，無諸過罪。
items.en: Because one holds a portion simply through faith and understanding, then, towards what is extremely profound and beyond one's own present, meager insight, one looks up to the Tathāgata, saying: this teaching belongs to the Buddha's own domain, not to my own present reach. In this way one gives rise to no slander of the teaching, does no harm to oneself, avoids the resulting misfortune, and incurs no fault at all.

items.zh: 由諸菩薩思惟法時，但依其義不依文故，於佛世尊一切所說密意語言，能隨悟入。
items.en: Because bodhisattvas, when reflecting on the teaching, rely on the meaning and not on the literal wording, they are able to enter directly into all of the World-Honoured Buddha's own statements spoken with hidden intent.

items.title: Section: Unshakeable Resolve, the First Breakthrough, and Its Stabilisation — Correct Thinking Concludes

items.zh: 由諸菩薩普於一切黑說、大說得善巧故，於真實義，無物無法能傾能動。
items.en: Because bodhisattvas become skilled across the whole of both the implicit and the explicit teaching, regarding genuine truth, no thing and no phenomenon whatsoever can shake or move them.

items.zh: 是諸菩薩正能悟入初思惟故，能得先來所未得忍。是諸菩薩，由即於此已所得忍，數數作意令堅牢故，能於其修隨順趣入。菩薩由是八種相故，能正修行正思所攝法隨法行。
items.en: Because bodhisattvas genuinely break through into a first reflection, they attain an acceptance of the truth never before attained. ... Because bodhisattvas, resting on this very acceptance already attained, apply repeated attention so that it becomes firm and stable, they are thereby able to enter in accordance with meditative cultivation. Through these eight marks, bodhisattvas are able to rightly practice the aspect of practising in accordance with the dharma comprised by correct thinking.

items.title: Section: Correct Cultivation Opens — Four Stages From Calm to Its Joyful Mastery

items.zh: 云何菩薩於法正修？當知此修、略有四相。一者、奢摩他，二者、毘鉢舍那，三者、修習奢摩他、毘鉢舍那，四者、樂修習奢摩他、毘鉢舍那。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's correct cultivation regarding the dharma? This cultivation should be understood as, in brief, four aspects: first, calm-abiding; second, insight; third, cultivating calm-abiding and insight together; fourth, delighting in cultivating calm-abiding and insight.

items.title: Section: What Calm-Abiding Actually Is — Resting the Mind Beyond All Words, Through Nine Stages

items.zh: 云何奢摩他？謂諸菩薩，由八種思善依持故，於離言說唯事、唯義所緣境中，繫心令住。離諸戲論、離心擾亂想作意故，於諸所緣而作勝解。
items.en: What is calm-abiding? Bodhisattvas, resting on the eight kinds of wholesome reflection already described, bind the mind so it remains fixed within a sphere of experience free of conceptual language, grasped as sheer fact and sheer meaning alone. Free of all conceptual proliferation, free of the disturbed, agitated attention that ordinarily accompanies perception, they arrive at a firm, confident grasp of whatever is taken as the object.

items.zh: 於諸定相，令心內住、安住、等住，廣說乃至一趣、等持。是名奢摩他。
items.en: Regarding the marks of meditative absorption, one causes the mind to be inwardly settled, stably settled, evenly settled, and so on in full detail up through single-pointed and fully sustained absorption. This is called calm-abiding.

items.title: Section: What Insight Actually Is — Investigating Reality Until Wisdom Fully Unfolds

items.zh: 云何毘鉢舍那？謂諸菩薩，由奢摩他熏修作意，即於如先所思惟法思惟其相。如理簡擇、最極簡擇、極簡擇法，廣說乃至覺、明、慧行。是名毘鉢舍那。
items.en: What is insight? Bodhisattvas, having cultivated the attention infused by calm-abiding, reflect on the character of exactly the teaching already reflected on before. Rightly discerning, most thoroughly discerning, and discerning the phenomenon in full — and so on in detail up through discernment, clarity, and wisdom in action. This is called insight.

items.title: Section: Calm and Insight United, Their Joyful Mastery, and Practising in Accordance With the Dharma Concludes

items.zh: 云何修習奢摩他、毘鉢舍那？謂諸菩薩，於奢摩他、毘鉢舍那，無間加行、殷重加行，恒常修習，是名修習奢摩他、毘鉢舍那。
items.en: What is cultivating calm-abiding and insight together? Bodhisattvas, applying themselves to calm-abiding and insight without interruption and with earnest care, cultivate them constantly. This is called cultivating calm-abiding and insight together.

items.zh: 云何樂修習奢摩他、毘鉢舍那？謂諸菩薩，即於如是止觀相中，其心無動，於無功用離諸加行任運轉處攝受無亂，是名樂修習奢摩他、毘鉢舍那。
items.en: What is delighting in cultivating calm-abiding and insight? Bodhisattvas, precisely within this state of calm and insight, hold the mind unmoving, gathering it without disturbance into a spontaneous flow requiring no exertion and no special effort at all. This is called delighting in cultivating calm-abiding and insight.

items.zh: 當知此中，是諸菩薩，如如修習奢摩他、毘鉢舍那，如是如是樂住奢摩他、毘鉢舍那；如如樂住奢摩他、毘鉢舍那，如是如是奢摩他、毘鉢舍那清淨。
如如奢摩他清淨，如是如是身安、心安增長廣大；如如毘鉢舍那清淨，如是如是若智、若見增長廣大。齊此名為修所應作，謂於所依中，應除遣麁重；及於一切所知，應修清淨智見。如是一切修所作業，菩薩由前四種修相，皆能成辦。
items.en: As calm-abiding grows purer, so too does the body's and mind's ease grow and expand; as insight grows purer, so too does knowledge and vision grow and expand. This much is called the task cultivation should accomplish — namely, removing the coarse habitual tendencies within body and mind, and cultivating pure knowledge and vision towards all that is known. All of this task of cultivation, bodhisattvas can accomplish through these four aspects just described.

blocks.text: How the bodhisattva practises what they have learned: in conduct, in reflection, and in meditation.

Body, speech, and mind act in accordance with the Dharma; one reflects correctly; one cultivates correctly. "What the Buddha prohibited one does not do; what he permitted one does." Ten perceptions steady practice (as on Day 239).

"Bodhisattvas dwell alone in quiet, and delight in reflecting on, weighing, and observing what they have heard." They avoid what should not be speculated about. "For one portion they understand through reasoned observation; for another, they simply hold it through faith."

Towards what is beyond their present insight, "they look up to the Tathāgata, saying: this teaching belongs to the Buddha's own domain". "Relying on the meaning, not the literal words, they enter the Buddha's statements spoken with hidden intent." Master Cháng Bǎi explains "reticent" and "great" teaching.
Skilled in both implicit and explicit teaching, "no phenomenon can shake them". Breaking through to "an acceptance of the truth never before attained", they stabilise it.

Four aspects: calm; insight; both together; and delight in them. **Calm**: "fixing the mind on a sphere free of conceptual language, sheer thing and sheer meaning", through the nine stages. **Insight**: "with attention infused by calm, reflecting on the teaching", discerning thoroughly. **Both**: "without interruption, with earnest care". **Delight**: "holding the mind unmoving, in a spontaneous flow". "As calm grows purer, ease grows; as insight grows purer, knowledge and vision grow." Venerable Miào Jìng: knowing is conventional wisdom; seeing, ultimate.

quiz.q: Practising in accordance "has five aspects." The English counts "as sought" and "as received" separately. How does Master Cháng Bǎi count?
options: body, speech, mind are three; thinking and cultivation two — five
quiz.why: "This practice is, in brief, of five kinds: as sought, as received, body, speech, and mind turning without error; correct thinking and correct cultivation." Master Cháng Bǎi: practising in accordance totals five — body, speech, and mind are three; correct thinking and correct cultivation two. ("As sought, as received" only qualify them.) The English counts differently.

quiz.q: Correct thinking "dwelling alone in quiet." What example does Venerable Miào Jìng give?
options: a monk living alone in his own room — that's dwelling alone in quiet
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas, dwelling alone in quiet, delight in reflecting on, weighing, and examining whatever they've heard." Venerable Miào Jìng: a monk living alone in a room — that's dwelling alone in quiet.

quiz.q: "Truly knowing 默說 and 大說." How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain 默說?
quiz.why: "They truly know the reticent teaching and the great teaching." Master Cháng Bǎi: 默說 refers to the hearer vehicle's provisional, non-definitive teaching.

quiz.q: "Relying on meaning, not words, they enter the Buddha's hidden intent." What examples of hidden intent do the masters give?
options: Cháng Bǎi: "killing father and mother attains arhatship" means killing ignorance and craving; Miào Jìng: dependent nature exists, imputed nature is empty — emptiness and existence don't obstruct each other
quiz.why: "Because, in reflecting on the Dharma, they rely on meaning and not words, they can enter all the Buddha's speech of hidden intent." Master Cháng Bǎi: the true meaning is killing the father, ignorance, and the mother, craving. Venerable Miào Jìng: the dependent nature exists by dependent origination; the imputed nature is utterly empty — emptiness doesn't obstruct existence, nor existence emptiness.

quiz.q: The first of four aspects, calm-abiding — what is its object, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: cultivating concentration on a non-discriminating image
quiz.why: "This cultivation has, in brief, four aspects: calm-abiding; insight; cultivating calm and insight; and delighting in cultivating them." Master Cháng Bǎi: first, calm-abiding — cultivating concentration with a non-discriminating image as object.

quiz.q: Calm-abiding fixes the mind "on the object of mere thing and mere meaning, beyond words." What is the object, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas, well supported by the eight kinds of thinking, fix the mind on the object of mere thing and mere meaning, beyond words." Venerable Miào Jìng: taking the dependent and perfected natures as object.

quiz.q: "As insight purifies, knowing and seeing grow vast." How do the masters distinguish knowing and seeing?
options: Miào Jìng: knowing is conventional wisdom, seeing ultimate; Cháng Bǎi: knowing concerns past and future, seeing the present
quiz.why: "As insight grows purified, so knowing and seeing grow vast." Venerable Miào Jìng: "knowing" is conventional wisdom; "seeing" is ultimate wisdom. Master Cháng Bǎi: knowing is wisdom about past and future; seeing is wisdom about the present. Their divisions differ.
